topics: KMS options: customer-managed keys (BYOK) vs Redwood-managed
Data residency and private deployment considerations
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-21 16:00 PST | Duration ~52 min | Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Sofia (Helix Head of Security), Marcus (CTO), Lina (Lead Cloud Eng), Devon (Compliance)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're going to focus on encryption and key management today, so I'll hand to Ethan for the technical overview.
[00:18] Ethan: Great, thanks Ava. So high level, Redwood supports encryption in transit via TLS 1.2/1.3, mutual TLS for private endpoints, and encryption at rest for model artifacts, logs, and customer data. For KMS we have three modes: Redwood-managed keys, customer-managed keys in cloud KMS, and BYOK w/ HSM-backed keys.
[00:35] Sofia: Quick clarifying q, when you say BYOK, does that mean the keys never touch Redwood's control plane?
[00:45] Ethan: Right, for BYOK we integrate with your KMS — you rotate and control keys. We use envelope encryption: service-side data is encrypted with a data key, which is then encrypted with your master key in your KMS. For HSM mode we can support import or external key references depending on provider.
[01:05] Marcus: Are there any minimums or performance impacts for HSM-backed keys? We run high throughput inference so latency is critical.
[01:15] Ethan: Good point. With HSM-backed CMKs we do limit direct live calls to the HSM per token — so we use an ephemeral data key cache and hardware key to wrap/unwrap occasionally. In practice the HSM calls are in the key lifecycle path, not per-request, so latency impact is minimal. We also support local key caching and key-encryption on host to avoid synchronous HSM round trips for every inference.
[01:40] Lina: Are you able to support Cloud HSM from multiple providers, we use both AWS KMS + AWS CloudHSM for some workloads and GCP KMS for others.
[01:52] Maya: Yes we have integrations for AWS KMS, CloudHSM, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault + HSM. For multi-region setups we can route encryption operations to the regional KMS to satisfy data residency.
[02:05] Devon: From audit standpoint we need immutable audit logs for key usage tied to the tenant. How do you expose key use and admin ops?
[02:15] Ethan: We emit audit logs to your log sink. For hosted we can push to customer-managed S3 or a log collector, and we include key operation events: create/import, wrap/unwrap, rotation, and KMS API calls. Those logs include request IDs and role principals. We can also forward to SIEM via CloudWatch, Stackdriver, or Splunk.
[02:40] Sofia: And for SOC 2 and FIPS, do you have certifications for the HSM or just references?
[02:48] Ava: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant — we'll share the report under NDA. For HSMs we rely on the hardware vendor's FIPS validations (e.g., AWS CloudHSM, Azure HSM) and our integration maintains the chain of custody.
[03:05] Marcus: About RBAC: we want separation between infra ops, dev, and security. Can you map roles to who can request key creation or rotate keys?
[03:15] Ethan: We support RBAC in the Console and via IAM role mappings. For BYOK scenario, the customer retains full control; Redwood will only be able to perform decrypt operations if you provision access. You can restrict admin operations to a security role. We also support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[03:38] Lina: If we go private (VPC/on-prem), does Redwood still need any key material?
[03:45] Maya: For Private deployments, you manage the KMS inside your network; Redwood's control plane can be run in a customer-managed VPC and we can optionally disable key escrow. In on-prem installs, keys never leave your environment unless you explicitly export.
[04:02] Sofia: Can you walk through a sample BYOK flow end-to-end?
[04:07] Ethan: Sure — step one: customer creates an asymmetric CMK or symmetric in their KMS and gives Redwood a key reference/ARN with restricted decrypt permission. Step two: Redwood requests a data key from the KMS, encrypts the data key with the CMK and stores the wrapped key alongside the data. Actual runtime uses the unwrapped data key which is cached in-memory on the host and ephemeral. On rotation, we call the KMS to rewrap new data keys and rotate the CMK per your policy.
[04:38] Marcus: So Redwood never stores plaintext CMKs and you only hold wrapped keys?
[04:44] Ethan: Correct — we never persist customer master keys in plaintext. We persist wrapped data keys and ephemeral unwrapped keys in volatile memory with strict TTLs and access controls.
[04:55] Lina: About key rotation cadence — we have a 90-day policy for some data classes, is your rotation automated?
[05:02] Maya: We can automate rotation with a policy; for BYOK you trigger rotation in your KMS and we pick up the new key references, or we can coordinate rotation windows and perform re-wrapping on a schedule you choose.
[05:18] Devon: For compliance we need proof of key origin and chain — can Redwood provide key attestation or HSM audit logs?
[05:27] Ethan: We can provide HSM attestation artifacts depending on provider: for example, CloudHSM has attestations and AWS KMS can provide key origin metadata. Redwood can surface those artifacts and include references in our audit logs.
[05:45] Sofia: Encryption in transit — you mentioned mTLS, is that required for private endpoints?
[05:51] Ethan: For private endpoints we strongly recommend mutual TLS. Customers can enforce client certs and rotate them via their cert authority. We also support VPC peering/private link options.
[06:05] Marcus: Any gotchas around KV cache or serving runtime that could leak sensitive prefixes? We use a lot of patient PII in prompts.
[06:14] Ethan: Good callout. Our runtime provides tenant isolation for KV cache; prefix caching is optional and we support per-tenant cache partitioning plus TTLs. For high-sensitivity workloads you can disable prefix caching and force fresh KV state per request. Also, logs can be redacted at ingestion to avoid PII capture.
[06:36] Lina: What about backups, are model checkpoints or data snapshots encrypted?
[06:41] Maya: All persistent storage is encrypted at rest. Backups are also encrypted and we can ensure the backup keys are customer-controlled in the BYOK model.
[06:50] Sofia: Incident response — if a key compromise is suspected, what's the emergency workflow?
[06:57] Ethan: We have a playbook: rotate keys, revoke access, switch to fallback model variant (we support automatic fallback to Redwood-managed key variants), and provide a forensics bundle with logs and KMS event traces. We'll also coordinate with your security team.
[07:17] Marcus: Is there an option to require HSM-backed key wrapping only for production? We want dev/test to be more flexible.
[07:24] Maya: Yes, you can configure env-specific key policies. Dev can use Redwood-managed keys, prod can require HSM-backed CMKs and strict rotation.
[07:38] Sofia: About proof: we'll need the SOC2 report, details on encryption algorithms (AES-256 GCM, RSA protections) and the list of endpoints that host keys.
[07:49] Ava: We'll send the SOC2 Type II, the crypto spec (algorithms, modes), and an architecture diagram showing where keys live across hosted/dedicated/private.
[07:58] Lina: Any integration hurdles with our existing KMS? We have strict IAM policies and cross-account access limited.
[08:05] Ethan: We support cross-account roles. The typical pattern is to create a service role in your account with minimal decrypt permissions and trust policy for Redwood's service principal. We can provide an IAM template.
[08:20] Devon: Audit retention — we need 7 years for some logs. Is that configurable?
[08:26] Maya: Yes, we can forward logs to your long-term storage. Redwood retention in hosted offering is configurable but long retention is usually done on your side for compliance.
[08:40] Sofia: Anything about hardware attestation for HSM? We need to verify HSM firmware and versioning.
[08:47] Ethan: We can surface vendor attestation data and firmware versions where available, and include that in the forensics bundle.
[08:57] Marcus: Is there any latency measurement you can share showing the impact of HSM-based BYOK on tail p99?
[09:04] Ava: We have benchmark spreadsheets — we'll share a sample, but as Ethan said the impact is usually in key lifecycle operations not per-token if caching is enabled.
[09:16] Sofia: One more on SSO and RBAC — can we map Azure AD groups to Redwood roles and limit key admin to a specific group?
[09:25] Maya: Yes, via SAML + SCIM provisioning you can map groups to roles and lock down key admin.
[09:33] Ava: Ok I want to summarize and next steps, we're going to send the SOC2 and KMS architecture doc plus the HSM checklist, Ethan will prepare IAM templates and an HSM integration checklist, and schedule a follow-up technical deep-dive next week for the infra team.
[09:48] Marcus: Sounds good.
[09:51] Sofia: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[09:54] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule.

End of transcript.

References noted during call: "KMS architecture doc (link)"; "SOC2 Type II (NDA)"; "HSM integration checklist (internal)"
